what_happened: The the person running Athena wrote request 0rz6, which renamed the final CI job to 'ci'. They did not check main's branch protection first. Branch protection requires a status check named 'fmt, clippy, tests'. With the job renamed, PR #314 could not merge because the required check never reported. The reader had also put branch protection out of scope. The the person running Athena queued job 20261031-085321-w7hj to give the job the required name and is running it by hand.
cause: Required status check names are host settings that live outside the repo. Neither the request writer nor the reader is shown them, and the reading treated branch protection as out of scope. Nothing compares a CI job name in a change against the required checks before the PR is opened. The failure appears only when the PR cannot merge. The same gap, writing about repository host settings without reading them, shows up in the existing host-settings class.
prevention: Add a check that runs when a request or reading touches CI workflow job names. It fetches main's required status checks from the host and verifies that each required name is still produced by a job in the changed workflow. If any is missing, it refuses the reading or plan. It also records the required check names in the reader's context so branch protection is not treated as out of scope when a job name changes.
proposed_request: Add a pre-dispatch check to Athena: when a reading, plan or diff changes the name of any job in a CI workflow file, fetch the required status checks of the target branch (main) from the repository host and confirm that each required name is still produced by a job in the changed workflows. If one is missing, refuse with a message naming the missing check. Also include the required check names in the reader's context so it does not treat branch protection as out of scope for CI renames. Acceptance: (1) a test where a workflow job is renamed away from a required name is refused and names the missing check; (2) a test where the required names are all still produced passes; (3) if the host's settings cannot be read, the check reports that it could not verify instead of passing silently; (4) the existing workflow, tests and changelog rules are unchanged.
